Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary: Adult patient with ~5 days of dry, hacking cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, intermittent headache, and chills. Denies hemoptysis, shortness of breath, and wheeze. Telemedicine exam notable for mild posterior pharyngeal erythema without tonsillar enlargement; no palpable neck glands reported. History significant for Type 2 diabetes mellitus (5–6 years) and mild hypertension. Home BP reportedly normal; home blood sugars reported stable.  
- Relevant differentials (from DDx, consistent with transcript):  
  - Viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) most consistent with symptom constellation and benign exam.  
  - Influenza and COVID-19 remain considerations given systemic symptoms and overlap.  
  - ACE inhibitor–induced cough considered less likely due to acute onset with coryzal symptoms.  
- Working diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory infection (common cold/nasopharyngitis).  
- Considerations: Influenza and COVID-19 (no testing performed or discussed); allergic rhinitis with postnasal drip less likely; ACE inhibitor–related cough unlikely given context.  
- Plan: Symptomatic management advised (paracetamol; OTC cold/flu combination remedies Day Nurse/Night Nurse deemed compatible with current medications). Safety-net advice: seek care if shortness of breath, wheeze, deterioration, or symptoms persist >3 weeks. No prescription issued.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Viral upper respiratory infection (High): Acute onset of dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, headache, and chills with mild throat erythema and no dyspnea/wheeze.  
- Influenza (Medium): Systemic symptoms compatible, though no documented fever and patient not systemically unwell.  
- COVID-19 (Medium): Symptom overlap (cough, myalgias, headache, chills, rhinorrhea), but no testing performed and no dyspnea or known exposure reported.
